items.headline: Six hurt as car driven by drug-driving suspect rear-ends a bus in Rochor
items.summary: A 31-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of drug-driving after his car rear-ended SBS Transit bus service 56 as it picked up passengers along Middle Road on Sep 12, Mothership reported. Six people on the bus were injured, and a vape was allegedly found in the car.

items.headline: Three Traffic Police officers investigated over unsafe riding caught on dashcam
items.summary: The Singapore Police Force said on Sep 13 that three of its Traffic Police officers are under investigation after dashcam footage filmed in Ubi appeared to show them riding in an unsafe manner, Mothership reported.

items.headline: MP warns Singapore is cutting itself too thin on food, producing under 10%
items.summary: In Parliament, MP Poh Li San questioned Singapore's resilience given it grows less than 10% of its own food, Mothership reported. She noted the country throws away about 790,000 tonnes of food a year, roughly 128kg per person.

items.headline: Singapore to raise political salaries; PM Wong to donate his own increase
items.summary: Parliament accepted a review committee's recommendation to lift political pay, with the reference salary for an entry-grade minister rising from S$1.1 million to S$1.8 million, Mothership reported. PM Lawrence Wong said he will donate his own increase to good causes for the next five years.

items.headline: India eases investment rules for bordering nations, reopening the door to China
items.summary: India's cabinet approved a fast-track mechanism to clear investments from land-bordering countries, including China, after a roughly six-year freeze, the South China Morning Post reported. Deals in areas such as capital goods, electronics and solar components will be processed within 60 days, provided Indian residents hold majority stakes.

items.headline: BRICS adopts the New Delhi Declaration as Modi hosts Putin and Xi
items.summary: Leaders adopted the New Delhi Declaration at the BRICS summit chaired by India, calling for restraint in the Middle East and reform of the UN Security Council, Al Jazeera reported. Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged the Global South to become a rule-shaper rather than a rule-taker.

items.headline: Modi urges Middle East dialogue as the US-Iran war lifts India's oil bill
items.summary: Meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the BRICS sidelines, Modi pressed for resolving the Middle East conflict through diplomacy, CNBC reported. India, which imports about 85% of its fuel, is among the economies most exposed to disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.headline: India's rupee slides to record lows as the oil surge strains the economy
items.summary: The rupee has weakened to record lows against the US dollar as the US-Iran war pushes up oil prices and portfolio outflows persist, the South China Morning Post reported, testing the bullish narrative around India's growth.

items.headline: UK economy unexpectedly grew 0.4% in July, offering Burnham some relief
items.summary: Britain's economy expanded 0.4% in July, beating forecasts, with artificial-intelligence activity helping lift output, Bloomberg reported. The surprise growth gives Prime Minister Andy Burnham a rare bright spot ahead of a difficult autumn Budget.

items.headline: Trump says a united Ireland would be fantastic, drawing UK pushback
items.summary: During a visit to Dublin, US President Donald Trump said he would love to see Ireland unified, CNN reported. Downing Street pointed to Burnham's position that a border poll is off the table, and the DUP's Gavin Robinson said Northern Ireland's future is for its own people to decide.

items.headline: Second crypto billionaire hands Reform UK a record £49m donation
items.summary: A second crypto billionaire has given Reform UK a record £49 million, Al Jazeera reported, sharpening a debate over party-funding rules that trade unions and MPs have urged Burnham to tighten.

items.headline: About 130 missing after a ferry capsizes in Indonesia's Java Sea
items.summary: A passenger ship carrying more than 240 people capsized in the Java Sea, and rescuers are searching for about 130 still missing, Al Jazeera and CNN reported. The vessel, bound from Surabaya to Borneo, lost contact early on Sep 13; more than 100 people have been rescued.

items.headline: Oil holds near six-week highs as the US-Iran tanker war chokes Hormuz
items.summary: Brent crude has climbed toward $100 a barrel as tit-for-tat US and Iranian attacks disrupt the Strait of Hormuz, Al Jazeera reported. Traffic through the chokepoint has fallen to roughly 10 ships a day, from about 130 before the war.

items.headline: Trump tells Zelenskyy to stop striking Russian energy supplies
items.summary: US President Donald Trump urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to halt attacks on Russian oil and diesel infrastructure, Al Jazeera reported, as strikes on refineries add to global fuel-price pressures.

items.headline: Sweden's centre-left opposition leads as the country votes
items.summary: A centre-left opposition bloc holds the lead in Sweden's election, according to polling cited by Al Jazeera, as voters weigh the cost of living and security.

items.headline: Apple unveils its first foldable iPhone, the $1,999 iPhone Duo
items.summary: Apple introduced its first foldable handset, the iPhone Duo starting near $2,000, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and AirPods 5, Bloomberg reported. The launch opened the tenure of new chief executive John Ternus, who succeeded Tim Cook.

items.headline: Microsoft maps a 26-gigawatt AI data-center buildout
items.summary: Microsoft is planning to add about 26 gigawatts of data-center capacity to meet AI demand after shortages forced it to turn away some cloud business, Bloomberg reported.

items.headline: Oracle's AI-cloud surge eases doubts over its data-center spending
items.summary: Oracle reported cloud-infrastructure revenue more than doubling and a fast-growing order backlog from AI customers, Bloomberg reported, easing concerns about its heavy build-out for clients including OpenAI and Nvidia.

items.headline: Fed seen all but certain to raise rates at its Sep 16 meeting
items.summary: Markets now price a roughly 90% chance the Federal Reserve raises rates on Sep 16 after August inflation came in hot at 3.4% year-on-year, CNBC reported. It would be the first hike of a possible tightening cycle, with the target range now 3.5%-3.75%.

items.headline: Wall Street rebounds Friday as the Dow adds about 509 points
items.summary: US stocks snapped a four-day slide on Sep 11, with the Dow up around 509 points (1.0%) to about 52,573, the S&P 500 up 0.9% and the Nasdaq up 1.0%, CNBC reported, as investors positioned for the coming Fed decision.

items.headline: Skyworks jumps 8% on plan to close its Qorvo takeover this year
items.summary: Chipmaker Skyworks Solutions rose more than 8% after saying it expects to complete its acquisition of rival Qorvo before year-end, CNBC reported; Qorvo shares gained about 5%.

items.headline: Oracle beats estimates as cloud revenue more than doubles
items.summary: Oracle posted adjusted earnings of $1.92 a share on revenue of $19.35 billion, topping forecasts, with cloud-infrastructure revenue more than doubling to $7.4 billion on AI demand, CNBC reported.

items.headline: 🎾 Zverev beats Shelton to win his first US Open title
items.summary: Alexander Zverev defeated American Ben Shelton 6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7, 6-2 to win the US Open men's final, his second Grand Slam title of 2026, ESPN reported.

items.headline: 🎾 Rybakina beats Sabalenka to win her first US Open and reclaim No. 1
items.summary: Elena Rybakina defeated Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 to win her first US Open women's singles title, ESPN reported, leaving New York as the world No. 1.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli wins the inaugural Madrid Spanish Grand Prix
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli won the first Spanish Grand Prix at Madrid's new Madring circuit, finishing ahead of Max Verstappen and Lando Norris after a Virtual Safety Car swung the race his way, Formula 1 reported. It was his eighth win of 2026, extending his championship lead.

items.headline: 🏏 India beat Afghanistan by 7 wickets to go 1-0 up in the T20I series
items.summary: India chased down 157 with seven wickets in hand in the first T20I in Delhi, Abhishek Sharma top-scoring with 82 off 32 balls, ESPNcricinfo reported. Jasprit Bumrah and Varun Chakravarthy marked returns from injury.

items.headline: 🏏 England complete a 3-0 sweep of Pakistan with an eight-wicket win
items.summary: England beat Pakistan by eight wickets in the third Test at Edgbaston to sweep the series 3-0, with Joe Root and Jordan Cox making unbeaten fifties, ESPNcricinfo reported.

items.headline: Weight-loss drug semaglutide extended lifespan in aged mice
items.summary: In a study published in Nature, elderly female mice given semaglutide — the drug in Ozempic and Wegovy — lived about 12% longer than untreated mice and showed better muscle and metabolic function, Scientific American reported. Researchers stressed the results are in mice, not people.

items.headline: A breakthrough pancreatic-cancer drug now shows promise against lung cancer
items.summary: Daraxonrasib, a RAS-blocking drug that nearly doubled survival in advanced pancreatic cancer and won early US approval in August, shrank tumours in more than 30% of non-small-cell lung cancer patients in a small trial, Nature and Scientific American reported.

items.headline: UN concedes the world will overshoot the 1.5°C warming limit
items.summary: A new UN Environment Programme assessment says exceeding the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C threshold is now unavoidable, with warming on track for about 1.8°C this century under current policies, Scientific American reported.

items.headline: Physicists show a quantum trick could build vast virtual telescopes
items.summary: Researchers demonstrated an entanglement-based technique that could let widely separated telescopes act as one giant instrument, sharply improving resolution, Scientific American reported — a proof of concept for quantum-enhanced astronomy.

fun_fact.headline: The inventor of the Pringles can was buried in one
fun_fact.body: The man who invented the Pringles can loved it so much that he was buried in one. Fredric Baur, a Procter & Gamble chemist, designed the tubular container and the way the curved chips stack inside it, filing the patent in 1966. When he died in 2008, his family honoured his wish and placed part of his ashes in a Pringles can — the original flavour — before burying it.

puzzle.title: Count the Squares
puzzle.body:
The figure below is a grid 4 squares wide and 4 squares tall (16 small squares in all):

┌─┬─┬─┬─┐
├─┼─┼─┼─┤
├─┼─┼─┼─┤
├─┼─┼─┼─┤
└─┴─┴─┴─┘

How many squares of ANY size can you find in this figure?
puzzle.approach: Do not stop at the small squares — larger squares overlap them. Count every size, from 1×1 up to the whole grid.
puzzle.answer:
30 squares.

Count them by size:
• 1×1 squares: 16
• 2×2 squares: 9
• 3×3 squares: 4
• 4×4 square: 1

16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 30.  (In an n×n grid the total is 1² + 2² + … + n².)

word_puzzle.title: Cooling Off
word_puzzle.body:
Turn WARM into COOL in five steps, changing one letter at a time. Every word in between must be valid.

WARM → _ _ _ _ → _ _ _ _ → _ _ _ _ → _ _ _ _ → COOL
word_puzzle.approach: Change exactly one letter at each step, and every rung must be a real English word.
word_puzzle.answer:
WARM → WARD → WORD → WOOD → WOOL → COOL

Each step changes a single letter: WARM→WARD (M→D), WARD→WORD (A→O), WORD→WOOD (R→O), WOOD→WOOL (D→L), WOOL→COOL (W→C).

Sports: US Open finals (Zverev def. Shelton; Rybakina def. Sabalenka) and the inaugural Madrid Spanish GP (Antonelli) are current results within the window; Madrid is the current round, not a stale recap.
Most items are effectively single reachable-source given the environment; summaries use attributed, conservative phrasing and risky superlatives were trimmed.
